proposals.before: The civil track had relied only on Left Secretariat recommendations. In Huangtong 8 (1148) provincial ministers said, "If we only follow the old precedent for recommendations, in time good and bad will not be distinguished and opportunism will multiply."
proposals.after: The civil track had relied only on Left Secretariat recommendations. In Emperor Xizong's Huangtong 8 (1148) provincial ministers said, "If we only follow the old precedent for recommendations, in time good and bad will not be distinguished and opportunism will multiply."
proposals.reason: Chinese names Emperor Xizong (熙宗) as the Huangtong 8 reign context; the idiomatic English omits him.

proposals.before: In Dading 29 (1189) those who reached Pacifier of the Realm required an imperial order for further promotion.
proposals.after: In Zhangzong's Dading 29 (1189) those who reached Pacifier of the Realm received an imperial order for promotion thereafter.
proposals.reason: Chinese opens with Zhangzong (章宗); the idiomatic English drops the named ruler present in the source and literal.

decisions.reason: s0181 has 至熙宗皇統八年; the idiomatic omits 熙宗, and restoring "Emperor Xizong's" before Huangtong 8 is accurate and natural.

decisions.after: In Zhangzong's Dading 29 (1189) those who reached Pacifier of the Realm required an imperial order for further promotion.
decisions.reason: s0163 opens 章宗大定二十九年, so the omitted ruler must be restored; but 取旨升除 means promotions require obtaining an imperial order, and the proposal's "received…thereafter" wrongly softens that procedural force—keep the original "required…for further promotion."

sourceWitness.excerpt: 章宗大定二十九年，遷至鎮國者取旨升除後
